body_rows.text: Genome-wide association studies have established a highly polygenic architecture for Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis [1,2]. Most risk variants lie outside protein-coding exons and canonical splice sites, implicating regulatory variation [3,4]. Fine-mapping narrows many loci to compact credible sets [5,6], and credible-set membership provides the starting point for regulatory annotation, target-gene assignment and macrophage-state interpretation.

IBD fine-mapping results were obtained from the Open Targets Platform GraphQL API on 12 November 2026 [7]. The primary discovery study was GCST90292538, a combined IBD GWAS across East Asian and European ancestries (45,106 cases and 353,562 controls). Crohn-specific (GCST90446792), ulcerative-colitis-specific (GCST90446794) and three 2017 phenotype-companion studies (GCST004131, GCST004132 and GCST004133) were used for locus-context comparison. The 2017 datasets overlap with the de Lange/IIBDGC samples incorporated into the Liu 2023 meta-analysis. All analyses used GRCh38 coordinates.

Credible-set membership, PIP, effect size, standard error and L2G predictions were downloaded through the Platform API. The primary set required PIP >= 0.1 and 95% credible-set membership [8]. Variants annotated as missense, synonymous, stop-gained, stop-lost, start-lost, frameshift, inframe insertion/deletion, protein-altering, splice acceptor, splice donor or splice-region were excluded.

A healthy pan-gastrointestinal myeloid atlas containing 33,213 cells [9] was filtered to adult control macrophages (level_2_annot = Macrophage, control_vs_disease = control, n_counts >= 1,000). Colorectal and ileal pools each contained 256 cells. At most eight cells per donor were included in the initial draw and iterative balancing reduced donor imbalance. Raw integer counts were obtained from .raw.X, and genes were represented by Ensembl identifiers for AlphaGenome conditioning. SC_GENE_EXPRESSION_DENOISED was the primary conditioned scorer.

Three additional public myeloid resources were used for activity-state evaluation [10,11]. Oliver 2024 active macrophages were colorectal level_2_annot = Macrophage cells annotated as ulcerative colitis or IBD; healthy comparators were normal colorectal macrophages. Kong 2023 active macrophages required cell_type = macrophage, disease = Crohn disease and Type = Infl. Controls required Type = Heal and normal disease. Garrido-Trigo 2023 active cells were Crohn or ulcerative colitis myeloid cells, with normal myeloid cells as controls.

Each activity or control pool contained 256 cells selected with round-robin donor balancing. Minimum raw UMI count was 300 where available. Oliver and Kong counts were recovered from .raw.X; Garrido-Trigo counts were obtained from integer .X. Full candidate scoring was performed in Oliver conditions; the top 28 variants and positive control were scored in Kong and Garrido pairs. Direction concordance required sign agreement after a 0.001 numerical tolerance. Effects with maximum absolute activity-state magnitude below 0.005 were classified as attenuated. Persistent support required the same direction with interpretable magnitude in active Oliver and at least one additional active cohort [12]. Six resampled donor-balanced pools were generated for PRKCQ to quantify sampling stability within the available donor pools.

The six initial Open Targets studies overlap at the publication and sample level. External support was rebuilt from UK Biobank WGS 2025 (GCST90473822, GCST90473823 and GCST90473826) [13] and MVP 2024 (GCST90480318, GCST90480319 and GCST90480320) [14]. Multiple phenotypes within one cohort were aggregated into one cohort-level support value.

GTEx v10 single-tissue eQTL results were queried for each Tier 1 variant and nominated target in sigmoid and transverse colon. A pair was retained only when the queried variant identifier and ALT allele matched. Myeloid eQTL and colocalization analyses used the published immune-cell and QTL frameworks [15,16].

GSE229472 macrophage MPRA counts were analyzed separately in three sequence contexts [17,18]. Risk-versus-nonrisk effects were calculated from log2 normalized reporter output using all eight RNA pools and the mean of four DNA pools per construct.

GSE327124 myeloid CRISPR screen counts were normalized within donor and sorted TNF-high/TNF-low or CD80-high/CD80-low bins [19]. Guide effects were calculated as log2((high + 1)/(low + 1)), averaged across donors and summarized as the median across at least three sgRNAs. An empirical null used 50,000 resamples of four guide effects. Gene-level P values were adjusted by Benjamini-Hochberg. TNF and TNFAIP3 were directional controls.

GSE327644 Perturb-seq H5 matrices were processed from four donors in resting and LPS states [20]. Cells were assigned when the dominant guide had at least five UMIs and the second guide had at most half the dominant count. Gene counts were aggregated to guide-by-sample pseudobulk and converted to log2 CPM using full gene-library depth. Each guide profile was compared with the matched non-targeting control in the same donor and state. Differential effects used paired t tests across donors and Benjamini-Hochberg correction within target and state. Empirical pathway tests resampled gene sets of equal size from expressed genes 10,000 times. TNF and TNFAIP3 served as directional downstream-response controls; targets with weak self-transcript reduction were assigned to a transcript-validation class.

GSE175685 processed THP-1 overexpression data were downloaded from GEO [21]. Target expression and transcriptome responses were compared with 11 empty-vector controls using Welch tests and Benjamini-Hochberg correction. For growth-sensitivity analysis, a sample-level principal component was derived from MSigDB Hallmark E2F Targets, G2-M Checkpoint, Myc Targets V1 and Myc Targets V2 genes. Gene expression was residualized on this component across all target and control samples. The GSEA workflow was then repeated with the same libraries, set-size limits, 1,000 permutations and seed.

We queried eight monocyte or macrophage eQTL datasets from the eQTL Catalogue [22,23]. These included Alasoo 2018 macrophages, BLUEPRINT monocytes, Nedelec 2016 macrophages, Quach 2016 monocytes and Schmiedel 2018 monocytes [24,25]. Additional single-cell and immune-cell QTL resources were retained for context [26,27]. ERGIC1, GCKR, ABCB5 and IRF2BP2 showed nominal P > 0.05 across queried myeloid datasets. CAMK2A rs1549913 showed a nominal IFN-gamma macrophage eQTL (P = 0.008; beta = -0.37). Its direction contrasted with AlphaGenome, and the Bonferroni value across 40 tests was approximately 0.310.

The main contribution is an evidence ladder that integrates genetic plausibility, model prediction, cell-context specificity, independent validation and causal inference. Fine-mapping establishes variant plausibility after LD [28,29]. Atlas calibration establishes whether a predicted effect is unusual against common variation [30,31]. Live and donor-conditioned models address different cell-context questions. These axes provide complementary evidence dimensions [32,33].

The ETS2 and IL2RA controls justify the ladder. ETS2 had a strong Atlas score and a reproducible macrophage direction across colon, ileum and donor-derived conditioning [34]. IL2RA also had an extreme Atlas score, but its live macrophage effect was nearly zero. A score-only workflow would promote both loci. The macrophage contrast recovered the intended cell-context distinction.

Previous IBD studies used fine-mapping and chromatin evidence to prioritize credible variants. Single-cell studies refined macrophage states in disease [35,36]. Reporter and CRISPR resources added experimental anchors [37,38], including primary myeloid screens [39]. The ladder integrates these complementary evidence types: reporter effect, gene-level perturbation and allele-specific causal effect each inform a distinct layer.

Among the Top 10, PDGFB is the leading macrophage-regulatory archetype. Its variant lies in an exact DC-macrophage cCRE linked to PDGFB [40]. The accessibility signal is enriched in a macrophage/DC topic. CRISPR and Perturb-seq data also show a measurable gene-level response. External UKB and MVP target-level L2G support contributed zero cohorts, while model, chromatin and perturbation evidence supported the candidate. The causal nucleotide at rs2143178 defines the next allele-resolved experiment.

Among the Top 10, PRKCB is the mechanistic-triangulation archetype. Its risk allele is associated with higher monocyte expression [41]. The GTEx sigmoid-colon eQTL provides a tissue-context contrast. THP-1 overexpression changes gene-expression programs, including inflammatory terms that are sensitive to growth state. IVW and weighted-median MR were positive, SMR was significant and SuSiE-colocalization reached H4 = 1.0. MR-Egger and HEIDI-style analyses define the sensitivity profile of the multi-instrument model. Shared credible-set signal and context-dependent effects support mechanistic follow-up.

PRKCQ, IL23R and CAMK2A provide complementary stress tests for the ladder. PRKCQ had attenuated transcript effects with reproducible LPS pathway suppression. IL23R is assigned to transcript-level validation through its guide-level self-transcript response. CAMK2A combined a nominal eQTL with colocalization-sensitivity analysis [42]. These results define the specific experimental assays for each candidate.
